title: Tri-Link Recursive Site Expansion Framework
purpose: To recursively map a website by selecting three associated links from a seed page, then repeating the same selection process on each discovered page for a fixed number of rounds while preserving entity and relationship structure.

core_definition.summary: A bounded recursive website exploration framework that expands outward from a starting page by selecting the three most relevant associated links from each page and repeating the process for up to 20 rounds.

objectives: Map site structure in a controlled and reproducible way
Surface real linked entities rather than abstract concepts where possible
Preserve traversal depth and discovery order
Support investigative, institutional, or research-oriented website analysis

association_policy.selection_goal: Select the three most relevant associated links from each page.

selection_priority.rule: Prefer internal links directly referenced in the main page body or primary navigation.
Prefer links that represent real entities, services, departments, programs, reports, locations, or named substructures.
Prefer links that deepen the current topical or institutional branch.
Prefer links with the strongest contextual relevance to the current page.
If more than three links qualify, choose the most specific and information-dense three.

exclusions: pure search-result pages unless explicitly needed
generic legal/footer pages unless directly relevant
